title: Nursing Home Roommate Effects on Mortality
discussion_signal: The NBER announcement presents roommate assignment as a low-cost social and institutional mechanism: peer effects can be comparable to differences across facilities, and better assignments may reduce mortality without additional staffing. It expands care quality beyond provider inputs to resident-to-resident exposure.
linked_research_question: How do roommate assignment, cognitive and behavioral peer characteristics, facility quality, staffing, and resident sorting interact to change mortality and unequal exposure in nursing homes?
limits: The announcement reports a bounded study result, not a universal assignment rule
Roommate matching may involve operational, ethical, and consent constraints
Public discussion does not establish implementation feasibility or effects across all facilities
